title: The Cutting Efficiency of a Hybrid Phacoemulsification Tip Using High and Low Intraocular Pressure Settings in Different Grades of Cataract

indication: Bilateral age-related cataract, LOCS III grade 3 or 4 (31 patients grade 3, 20 grade 4), adults aged 50 years or older; pseudoexfoliation, zonular dehiscence, eye trauma, rheumatoid arthritis and prior refractive surgery excluded

groups.description: Phacoemulsification with the Centurion Vision System, Active Sentry handpiece and Intrepid hybrid tip at high IOP settings (target IOP 50-65 mmHg by step, higher vacuum and aspiration; Table 1); one randomized eye of each patient, one surgeon
Same platform, handpiece, tip and surgeon at low IOP settings (target IOP 20 mmHg, lower vacuum and aspiration in quadrant removal; Table 1); the operated contralateral eye of the same patients

exclusions.what: t0004 IOP rows, t0002 IOP, age and sex rows, t0001 and t0003 (machine settings and operative data)

notes: Prospective randomized contralateral-eye study (NCT05868772): one eye at high and the fellow eye at low IOP settings, 51 patients / 102 eyes completed; both eyes were operated, so the arms are not independent samples and neither is an unoperated fellow eye.

Role: both arms use the same commercially available platform, handpiece and hybrid tip at two fluidic settings; the article does not declare an experimental arm (Introduction frames lower IOP settings as potentially reducing postoperative complications), so both arms are recorded as control (separate groups).
CCT measurement method is not stated anywhere in the article; method recorded as 'unstated'.
Value kind cct_change: Table 4 reports only the change from the preoperative CCT; the preoperative CCT of the same arm is cited from Table 2 as the reference.
Three IOP-related adverse events resolved within a week (Results); not used. Study supported by an Alcon investigator-initiated grant.
